authors: Baek, C., Jiang, Y., Raghunathan, A. & Kolter, J.Z.
title: Agreement-on-the-line: Predicting the performance of neural networks under distribution shift
source: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS 2022) (arXiv:2206.13089)
relevance: Estimates out-of-distribution ACCURACY using only UNLABELLED target data plus the predictions of several models, by exploiting that OOD agreement between any two networks correlates linearly with their in-distribution agreement. That is a direct answer to our hardest practical question - how good is the model on 2002, where no trustworthy label exists - and it needs nothing we do not already have: 18 unlabelled years and multiple trained per-year models. Crucially it is self-checking: the phenomenon holds whenever accuracy-on-the-line holds, and that condition can itself be tested from unlabelled data, so we would learn whether our years are even amenable before trusting any estimate.

authors: Wang, L., Wang, J., Wang, Y. & Xie, X.
title: Towards optimization and model selection for domain generalization: A mixup-guided solution
source: Proceedings of the 2024 SIAM International Conference on Data Mining (SDM), 244-252
relevance: Takes seriously the problem Gulrajani & Lopez-Paz (ID 151) raised and we inherited - that DG model selection is usually unstated or covertly uses target data - and proposes selecting without touching the target domain. Directly relevant to open question Q33: our current selection on projected 2020 labels is a proxy carrying the training signal's own bias, and this gives a published alternative to compare against leave-one-era-out. Peer-reviewed and short; read before fixing our selection rule rather than inventing one.
